LanguageData.MST.rootSelectionWeightComment: Base weight for random selection (weighted random, not a chance). The sum of all weights in the same pool is the denominator; 0 removes the quest from the random pool.
LanguageData.MST.rootSelectionWeightFactorFromPointsC: Scales the weight above by colony points: X is points, Y is a multiplier. An empty curve adds nothing; values beyond the ends use the end value.
LanguageData.MST.rootMinPointsComment: Below this colony points value the quest's weight becomes 0, so it never appears.
LanguageData.MST.rootMinProgressScoreComment: Below this progress score the weight becomes 0. Progress score is derived by the storyteller from days, population and wealth — it is not threat points.
LanguageData.MST.rootEarliestDayComment: Earliest day after landing on which this quest can be picked.
LanguageData.MST.minRefireDaysComment: Minimum days before the same quest can appear again. Its weight is 0 during that window; 0 means no limit.
LanguageData.MST.expireDaysRangeComment: How long (in days, randomly picked in the range) the offer can be accepted. -1~-1 means it never expires.
LanguageData.MST.autoAcceptComment: The quest is accepted automatically when it appears — the player never clicks accept and cannot decline. Mutually exclusive with ExpireDays: having both makes vanilla log a config error for the def (logged only, harmless); this page does not block it.
LanguageData.MST.decreeSelectionWeightComment: Selection weight for Royalty decrees. Independent of the random pool. 0 means it never appears as a decree.
LanguageData.MST.defaultChallengeRatingComment: Challenge rating of the quest, which picks the pawn count and the tier of negative events (1 lightest, 3 heaviest). -1 means unset — the generation defaults apply.
LanguageData.MST.randomlySelectableComment: Whether the quest may be picked at random. When off it never appears as a random quest even if its weight is non-zero (the weight is kept so you can re-enable it later).
LanguageData.MST.rootIncreasesPopulationComment: Whether this counts as a population-increasing quest. The game splits chance between the two pools by population intent, then rolls within each pool — the pools do not compete.
LanguageData.MST.canGiveRoyalFavorComment: Whether the quest can grant royal favor. While the player has a faction that grants favor, non-favor quests are down-weighted by a days-since curve; flagging it avoids that penalty.
